newsitem.title: FINLAND: EU approves Kesko's Tuko deal solution - STT.
newsitem.headline: EU approves Kesko's Tuko deal solution - STT.

text.p: The European Commission on Friday approved Finnish wholesaler and retailer Kesko Oy's proposed partial unwinding of last year's merger with domestic rival Tuko, the Finnish news agency STT reported.
In a statement, the Commission said: "The Commission is satisfied that the proposal allows for the restoration of effective competition on the Finnish markets and cash and carry sales of such goods."
"The Commission is satisfied that the proposal allows for the Tuko business to return to the same competitive condition as it held prior to Kesko's acquisition," it said.
Kesko's proposed partial unwinding of the merger came after the commission had blocked it in November, saying it distorted competition on the domestic retail and cash and carry sales markets.

The solution proposed by Kesko was to sell the operative part of Tuko's daily consumer goods business to Oy Stockmann Ab,, Sentra Oy, Wihuri Oy and Heinon Tukku Oy -- all companies with "extensive experience of the daily consumer business sector in Finland," the commission said.
Kesko would also sell some Tuko real estate to a consortium of insurance companies.

In a statement of its own, Kesko said the EU's decision meant that the agreed arrangements could take force. It said Tuko's Anttila Oy department store chain and Rautia Oy hardware stores would remain part of Kesko.
